description: Void visual governance contract for theme-sensitive surfaces. This is a validation checklist and coverage contract, not proof that visual screenshots or contrast reviews already passed.

surfaces.label: App shell and navigation

evidence.requirement: Theme-sensitive shell changes must keep the existing Web UI color-governance baseline clean.
Review desktop and narrow shell layouts after nav, background, border, or readable text token changes.

protectedContracts: Shell components only compose and render app state.
Session, provider, media, and short-drama business decisions stay outside shell rendering.
risks: System theme resolution can differ between browser and desktop webview.
Navigation state can hide selected and disabled contrast regressions.

surfaces.label: Flow Chat conversation surface

evidence.requirement: Flow Chat changes must not increase unresolved vars, fallback-only vars, or near-color debt outside the accepted baseline.
Review streaming, completed, background command, markdown, empty, and error states in dark and light themes.

protectedContracts: Flow Chat store remains the state boundary for conversation rendering.
Multi-agent, subdialog, and floating-window features must stay available.
risks: Streaming and virtualized entries can delay visible token regressions.
Tool cards combine card, status, markdown, and terminal color domains.

surfaces.label: Terminal and terminal tool card

evidence.requirement: Terminal colors must remain in terminal-specific domains instead of becoming generic app UI literals.
Review normal and bright ANSI colors against terminal background before merging terminal palette changes.

protectedContracts: Terminal UI remains isolated from provider and desktop process-control internals.
Terminal rendering does not own command execution policy.
risks: ANSI colors carry external semantic meaning and cannot be merged by numeric similarity alone.
Embedded terminal cards must satisfy both terminal and Flow Chat contrast expectations.

surfaces.label: Markdown, syntax, and Mermaid rendering

evidence.requirement: Markdown, Prism, and Mermaid colors must stay in syntax, mermaid, boundary, or token domains.
Review prose, links, tables, code blocks, and diagrams after markdown or embedded-renderer token changes.

protectedContracts: Markdown rendering stays a presentation boundary and must not infer session source.
Mermaid graph roles remain distinct from generic app status colors.
risks: Embedded content can resolve fallback colors before host variables are available.
Diagram roles do not map directly to app success, warning, or error colors.

surfaces.label: Generated widgets and iframe fallbacks

evidence.requirement: Review iframe fallback rendering and host-payload rendering whenever widget payload token contracts change.
Generated widget fallback colors must remain centralized and must not add untracked raw app colors.

protectedContracts: Generated widgets communicate through host payload contracts rather than mutating app internals.
Iframe first paint remains supported before host variables arrive.
risks: Fallback rendering can differ from host payload rendering.
Widget compatibility may require older aliases to stay exported while internal reads are reduced separately.

surfaces.label: AI media and short-drama canvas

evidence.requirement: Canvas, media, and short-drama surfaces must stay inside the Web UI theme-governance baseline.
Review asset grid, preview, empty, loading, and error states after media-canvas token or layout changes.

protectedContracts: Workspace media and short-drama state models remain separate from theme governance scripts.
Canvas UI must not take dependencies on CLI, installer, or desktop process internals.
risks: Media previews combine dense controls, asset thumbnails, and error states.
Short-drama workflow changes can hide theme regressions behind generated content availability.

surfaces.label: Mobile web shell

evidence.requirement: Mobile web theme changes must not increase the accepted mobile-web color-governance baseline.
Theme contract changes must not assume desktop-only WebView behavior or break mobile-web type checking.

protectedContracts: Mobile web remains a separate target with its own build and validation path.
Desktop-only theme runtime assumptions must not leak into mobile web.
risks: Mobile and narrow layouts expose spacing and contrast regressions that desktop screenshots can miss.
Mobile web may not exercise desktop webview theme bootstrap paths.

surfaces.label: Installer visual shell

evidence.requirement: Installer visual changes must stay within the accepted installer color-governance baseline.
Review progress, success, error, and permission states before merging installer visual changes.

protectedContracts: Installer naming and bundle identity remain Void-only.
Installer visual governance does not modify release workflow or packaging targets.
risks: Installer colors are validated separately from the Web UI baseline.
Packaging identity changes require a dedicated release workflow issue.
